erin_sec: Quick heads up — I'm proposing an RBAC tightening for the private keystore-proxy that'll go live TOM at 11:00 PT. Scope: remove broad `keystore:admin` binding from the legacy svcacct and replace with narrow `keystore:decrypt` + `keystore:sign` roles. Need quick sanity check for audit+netpol implications.

raj_sre: What's the blast radius? Any chance this causes automated restarts or eviction on Dedicated nodes?

mike_infra: It shouldn't trigger evictions — change is purely IAM on the proxy side. Concern is requests that fallback to legacy KMS path may start failing if we miss an allowlist. Need to ensure retry/fallback logs are clear.

sarah_prod: Will customers see 403s? We should prepare a customer-facing blurb if there's any surface risk.

erin_sec: Minimal risk for external users; internal automation that used the old svcacct could fail. We should capture `keystore.decrypt` failure events and tag them with `priv-deploy` metadata so SRE + support can search fast.

julia_ops: Can we log structured events to the audit pipeline? My ask: include `event_type`, `resource_id`, `caller_identity`, `decision_reason`, and `request_payload_sha256` for replay-proofing.

erin_sec: Agreed. Draft audit shape I'm proposing: `{ event_type: "keystore.decrypt_attempt", resource: "keystore-proxy/<pod>", actor: "svcacct/<name>", allowed: boolean, reason: "rbac|quota|netpol|kms-error", request_sha256: "..." }`. This goes to the local file auditlog and forwarded to SIEM.

mike_infra: Two network items: 1) netpols need to block pod egress to public KMS endpoints in priv mode; only allow to internal KMS gateway IPs. 2) conntrack/timeouts — tightened netpols sometimes flip ephemeral port ranges and kill long-lived streams (LLM KV cache sync). Can we add a conntrack exemption for the proxy?

erin_sec: For (1) good. We'll add `egress: allow -> kms-gateway:443` only. For (2) we can whitelist the proxy's namespace for longer conntrack TTLs via iptables conntrack settings on the node; will coordinate with eng-infra.

raj_sre: Also, how are we ensuring audit logs are tamper-evident for on-prem air-gapped customers? We can't rely on remote SIEM always.

erin_sec: For private/on-prem, we add a signed audit chain: each log chunk includes a HMAC with node-specific key, rotated monthly. The key is wrapped by the customer's HSM/KMS. We record key handle in metadata.

julia_ops: Need to make sure the key handle rotations themselves are auditable. Record `kms.rotate_key` events.

erin_sec: Yes. We'll add `kms.rotate_key` + `keystore.key_handle` to the audit stream.

kms-bot: ALERT: 2024-09-18T18:09:01Z — 1 failed decrypt from svcacct/legacy-batcher to keystore-proxy-3 (reason=rbac).

mike_infra: That alert is expected from the canary test we just ran. Good — we got a clean `reason=rbac` tag.

sarah_prod: Action items?

erin_sec: 1) eng-infra (mike) to add conntrack exemption + netpol egress rule. 2) ops (julia) to extend audit schema and wire HMAC signing for on-prem. 3) eng-sre (raj) to add SIEM parsers for new `keystore.decrypt_attempt` and `kms.rotate_key` events. 4) product to draft customer blurb if we see >5% failure rate post-rollout.

julia_ops: I'll put a quick runbook snippet in the ticket for how to validate signed chunks: `openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac $KEY < chunk.log > chunk.sig` and verify handle metadata.

raj_sre: Also adding a short incident play: if we see a spike of `reason=kms-error` fallback, auto-open a high-priority incident and rollback RBAC change to the broad svcacct while we triage.

erin_sec: Sounds good. I'll schedule the rollout and post the PR link. Posting checklist here once PR is open. :+1:
